title: Feelings and personality
focus: osshosti, osthir, obhiman, afsos, hingse, hotash, swarthopor, sohanubhuti, dhoirjo, mejaj, manoshik chap, nirbhorjoggo, oporadhbodh, mukhchora
body:
# Feelings and personality

You already have khushi, dukkho, rag and klanto. Adult conversation needs finer shades: the uneasy feeling in a room, the regret over a missed chance, the colleague who is dependable or arrogant. These words let you describe people and moods precisely.

| Romanization | Bengali | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| osshosti | অস্বস্তি | uneasy / awkward feeling (noun) |
| osthir | অস্থির | restless / agitated (can't sit still) |
| obhiman | অভিমান | hurt feelings / sulking at someone close (wounded pride) |
| onutap | অনুতাপ | remorse / repentance (formal) |
| afsos | আফসোস | regret / pity (that something didn't happen) |
| hingse | হিংসে | jealousy / envy (spoken) |
| hotash | হতাশ | disheartened / let down |
| jedi | জেদি | stubborn / obstinate |
| bhodro | ভদ্র | polite / decent / well-mannered (person) |
| swarthopor | স্বার্থপর | selfish |
| sohanubhuti | সহানুভূতি | sympathy / compassion |
| dhoirjo | ধৈর্য | patience |
| mejaj | মেজাজ | temper / mood (one's disposition right now) |
| manoshik chap | মানসিক চাপ | mental stress (formal) |
| uttejona | উত্তেজনা | excitement / tension (in the air) |
| nirbhorjoggo | নির্ভরযোগ্য | reliable / dependable (person or source) |
| attobishshash | আত্মবিশ্বাস | self-confidence |
| dushchinta | দুশ্চিন্তা | worry / anxiety (noun) |
| oprostut | অপ্রস্তুত | flustered / caught off guard |
| oporadhbodh | অপরাধবোধ | guilt / sense of guilt |
| binoyi | বিনয়ী | humble / modest |
| ohonkari | অহংকারী | arrogant / conceited |
| kouthuholi | কৌতূহলী | curious / inquisitive |
| mukhchora | মুখচোরা | shy / tongue-tied (won't speak up) |
| khitkhite | খিটখিটে | irritable / crabby |
| dhirsthir | ধীরস্থির | calm and composed (steady temperament) |
| mejaj harano | মেজাজ হারানো | to lose one's temper |
| gaye laga | গায়ে লাগা | to sting / hurt (of a remark, take it personally) |

## Which word?

- **obhiman vs rag**: rag is anger at anyone. obhiman is the hurt sulk you feel toward someone close who let you down. You don't feel obhiman toward a stranger.
- **onutap vs afsos**: onutap is moral remorse and sounds written. afsos is everyday regret over something you missed or didn't do.
- **osshosti vs osthir**: osshosti is discomfort or awkwardness; osthir is restlessness, being unable to settle.
- **hingse vs hingsa**: hingse is the spoken word for jealousy. হিংসা (hingsa) in news means violence. Keep them apart.
- **Loans**: Kolkata speakers freely say stress, tension, confidence, guilty, excited and awkward. The Bengali words are still used and sound more serious.

## Examples

- or samne kotha bolte amar osshosti lage: I feel uneasy talking in front of him
- ma-r upor obhiman kore o kotha bolchhe na: she's sulking at Mum and won't talk
- concert-ta miss korar afsos ekhono jayni: I still regret missing that concert
- interview-ta bhalo hoyni bole o khub hotash: he's disheartened because the interview went badly
- ektu dhoirjo dhoro, sob thik hoye jabe: be a little patient, it'll all work out
- aj boss-er mejaj bhalo nei: the boss is in a bad mood today
- o khub nirbhorjoggo, kaj-ta oke diye dao: he's dependable, give the job to him
- oke mitthe bole amar oporadhbodh hochchhe: I feel guilty for lying to her
- or kotha-ta amar gaye legechhe: what he said really stung
- o ektu mukhchora, meeting-e kichhu bole na: she's a bit shy, says nothing in meetings

cards.Example: or samne kotha bolte amar osshosti lage: I feel uneasy talking in front of him
cards.Notes: osshosti lage = I feel uneasy; also used for physical discomfort. People often just say 'awkward lagchhe'.

cards.Example: result-er aage o bhishon osthir hoye chhilo: she was really restless before the result
cards.Notes: osthir hoye jawa = to get worked up; osthirota = restlessness.

cards.English: hurt feelings / sulking at someone close (wounded pride)
cards.Example: ma-r upor obhiman kore o sokal theke kotha bolchhe na: she's been sulking at Mum since morning and won't talk
cards.Notes: obhiman is only toward someone close who should have known better; rag is plain anger.

cards.Example: nijer bhul-er jonno or kono onutap nei: he has no remorse for his mistake
cards.Notes: Written and serious. In conversation people say afsos or 'kharap lagchhe'.

cards.Example: concert-ta miss korar afsos ekhono jayni: I still regret missing that concert
cards.Notes: afsos is everyday regret over a missed chance; onutap is moral remorse.

cards.Example: or notun gari dekhe tomar hingse hochchhe na to?: you're not jealous of his new car, are you?
cards.Notes: Spoken form; written হিংসা. 'jealous' is also used as a loan.

cards.Example: interview-ta bhalo hoyni bole o khub hotash: he's very disheartened because the interview went badly
cards.Notes: hotasha = disappointment, also depression in the loose sense; nirash is similar but milder.

cards.Example: tumi bhishon jedi, kichhutei mante chao na: you're so stubborn, you never give in
cards.Notes: jed = stubbornness; jed dhora = to dig your heels in.

cards.Example: chhele-ta khub bhodro, sobar songe bhalo bhabe kotha bole: he's a very decent guy, talks nicely to everyone
cards.Notes: obhodro = rude; bhodrota = courtesy. Also used for 'respectable' (bhodro paray = in a decent neighbourhood).

cards.Example: eto swarthopor hoyo na, onnoder kotha-o bhabo: don't be so selfish, think about others too
cards.Notes: swartho = self-interest; nisswartho = selfless.

cards.Example: or obostha shune amar sohanubhuti hochchhe: I feel for him hearing about his situation
cards.Notes: sohanubhuti dekhano = to show sympathy. 'empathy' in English is often used for the deeper sense.

cards.Example: ektu dhoirjo dhoro, sob thik hoye jabe: be a little patient, it'll all work out
cards.Notes: dhoirjo dhora = to be patient; dhoirjo harano = to lose patience.

cards.Example: aj boss-er mejaj bhalo nei, pore kotha bolo: the boss is in a bad mood today, talk later
cards.Notes: mejaj kharap = in a bad mood; mejaji = moody, short-tempered.

cards.Example: ei mash-e khub manoshik chap jachchhe: it's been a very stressful month
cards.Notes: In speech 'stress' or 'tension' is more common; chap alone also works (khub chap-e achhi).

cards.Example: shesh over-e math-e bhishon uttejona chhilo: there was huge excitement at the ground in the last over
cards.Notes: Also means unrest or agitation in news (elaka-y uttejona). For personal excitement people often say 'excited'.

cards.Example: o khub nirbhorjoggo, kaj-ta oke diye dao: he's very dependable, give the job to him
cards.Notes: Casually: 'oke bhorsa kora jay' (you can count on him).

cards.Example: notun chakri-te ese or attobishshash bere geche: her confidence has grown since starting the new job
cards.Notes: 'confidence' is the common loan; attobishshash is used too, especially in serious talk.

cards.Example: eto dushchinta koro na, ami achhi to: don't worry so much, I'm here
cards.Notes: dushchinta = anxious worry; chinta can be just 'thought'. chintito = worried (adjective).

cards.Example: prosno-ta shune o ektu oprostut hoye gelo: he got a bit flustered at the question
cards.Notes: oprostut = unprepared and embarrassed in the moment; lojja is general shame or shyness.

cards.Example: oke mitthe bole amar oporadhbodh hochchhe: I feel guilty for lying to her
cards.Notes: Colloquially 'guilty feel korchhi' is very common.

cards.Example: eto boro chakri kore-o o khub binoyi: despite such a big job he's very humble
cards.Notes: binoy = humility. Opposite: ohonkari.

cards.Example: taka hoye o ekdom ohonkari hoye geche: since getting rich he's become really arrogant
cards.Notes: Spoken alternative: demaki (from demak, airs).

cards.Example: bachcha-ra sob byapare kouthuholi: kids are curious about everything
cards.Notes: kouthuhol = curiosity (amar kouthuhol hochchhe = I'm curious).

cards.Example: o ektu mukhchora, meeting-e kichhu bole na: she's a bit shy, doesn't say anything in meetings
cards.Notes: Kolkata word for someone who keeps quiet in company; lajuk is shy in a bashful way.

cards.Example: ghum na hole ami khitkhite hoye jai: I get crabby when I don't sleep
cards.Notes: Describes a grumpy, snappish temperament; ragi is simply quick to anger.

cards.Example: bipod-er somoy-o o dhirsthir thake: he stays composed even in a crisis
cards.Notes: Praise for a steady person; shanto is calm or quiet in general.

cards.Example: meeting-e mejaj haranor kono dorkar chhilo na: there was no need to lose your temper in the meeting
cards.Notes: Also: matha gorom kora (to get hot-headed), more casual.

cards.English: to sting / hurt (of a remark, take it personally)
cards.Example: or kotha-ta amar gaye legechhe: what he said really stung
cards.Notes: Literally 'to touch the body'. kotha gaye makha = to brush off remarks (the opposite).

cards.English: I'm under a lot of pressure right now.
cards.Notes: Natural spoken line; 'khub stress-e achhi' is equally common.

cards.English: I didn't mean to hurt you.
cards.Notes: kosto dewa = to hurt someone's feelings; apni form: apnake kosto dite chaini.
